items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 321-323 (book Lemma 3.3.4): every mere proposition is a set. The statement is a level implication and the proof (source lines 324-330) has to exhibit the uniformity of paths rather than merely assert it: it fixes a point and turns the propositionality proof into a function into the path family, applies the dependent action on paths of that function to an arbitrary path, computes the resulting dependent path through the transport rule in a path family to obtain an explicit equation expressing that path by two values of the auxiliary function, and then observes that any two loops at the point are given by the same expression. The transport computation is the core and it is not visible in the statement.
